articles.description: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 5 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週 ベッティングガイド：分析、おすすめの賭け方、日曜日のTD予測
articles.descriptionJa: 専門家が第5週のオッズやプレイヤープロップを徹底分析し、ベッティングのヒントや注目のプレーを紹介します。
articles.body:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value.

Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 5.

From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, the top game to bet, favorite defensive props to play and the top predicted TD scorers.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Bowen's Game of the Week

Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 44.5)

1 p.m. ET on CBS, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh

We need to have a bounce-back week here after betting on the Bills last Sunday. So, let's pivot to a rested Pittsburgh team that played Thursday night in Week 4 at home against an Indianapolis team straight off a London trip. We'll look at both sides of the ball, then hit some props from this game and across the league in Week 5.

When the Steelers have the ball: Running back Jaylen Warren has seen his usage (and production) elevate over the past two games. During this stretch (against Cincinnati and Cleveland) Warren has averaged 6.5 yards per carry, 21 touches and 151 scrimmage yards. He's also playing fast on the tape, and there's a lot of outside zone here, with Warren finding daylight. Plus, he's getting the ball on swings, screens and checkdowns. This is a good matchup for Warren against a Colts defense giving up 131 rushing yards per game (28th in the league). I expect a volume day for the Steelers' lead back.

The Colts' defensive numbers in the pass game point to a Pittsburgh edge as well, as the Colts are giving up 261.3 yards per game through the air and are pressuring the QB at a rate of only 28.3% (29th in the league). But can the Steelers protect and give Aaron Rodgers time and a clean pocket? Rodgers has three touchdown passes and six completions of 15 or more air yards in each of his past two games, but he has been sacked seven times during that stretch and a total of 13 times on the season (tied for most in the league). Rodgers' declining mobility also plays a role, but he needs the pocket to throw vertically to DK Metcalf and work the play-action pass game in Mike McCarthy's offense.

articles.headline: Kings lose Maxime Raynaud to apparent serious knee injury
articles.description: Kings second-year center Maxime Raynaud suffered what appeared to be a serious right knee injury in Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors.
articles.headlineJa: キングス、マキシム・レイノーが深刻な膝の負傷に見舞われる
articles.descriptionJa: キングスの2年目センター、マキシム・レイノーが土曜日のウォリアーズとのプレシーズンゲーム中に、右膝の深刻な負傷と思われる症状に見舞われました。
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings lost second-year center Maxime Raynaud after what appeared to be a serious right knee injury late in the first half of their preseason game at the Golden State Warriors on Saturday night.

Raynaud was setting a screen for rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. with Golden State's Stephen Curry in the vicinity defending it. As bodies collided, Raynaud took contact to the outside of his right knee, immediately yelling in pain and crumpling to the floor.

The seriousness of the situation became obvious quickly. Sacramento coach Doug Christie called timeout and walked out to the middle of the floor to check on Raynaud, who had his hands over his face. As teammates descended, team trainers called over the EMT with a wheelchair to help Raynaud to the locker room.

Raynaud spent halftime getting tests on the injury in Chase Center. The team officially ruled him out with a right knee injury early in the third quarter.

At that time, a dispirited Raynaud was wheeled from the X-ray room back to the area outside the visitors locker room. While there, Kings general manager Scott Perry and team owner Vivek Ranadive visited him. Ranadive gave Raynaud a hug, and team sources confirmed that there was a growing fear they've lost their young center for the foreseeable future.

The team did not have an official updated on Raynaud's injury after the game. He is expected to undergo an MRI late Saturday night. 

Raynaud made the All-Rookie second team last season after averaging 12.5 points and 7.5 rebounds in 74 games, proving to be a significant draft night find with the 42nd pick.

He was expected to play a key frontcourt role behind starting center Domantas Sabonis to open the season.

articles.headline: Source: Odell Beckham Jr. joins Vikings roster, status unclear
articles.description: While the Vikings elevated receiver Odell Beckham Jr. from the practice squad for Sunday's game, a source said, it's not yet decided if he'll play.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：オデル・ベッカムJr.がバイキングスのロースターに加入、出場状況は不透明
articles.descriptionJa: バイキングスは日曜日の試合に向けてレシーバーのオデル・ベッカムJr.をプラクティススクワッドから昇格させたが、情報筋によると、彼が出場するかどうかはまだ決まっていないという。
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have elevated receiver Odell Beckham Jr. from their practice squad for Sunday's game at the New Orleans Saints, a source said Saturday.

The team has not yet decided whether Beckham will be active and in unform, however. Coach Kevin O'Connell said Friday that if Beckham were elevated, his game status would likely depend on the health of receivers Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison. A source reiterated Saturday that remains the case. The Vikings also elevated receiver Jeshaun Jones from their practice squad.  

Neither Jefferson nor Addison had a full day of practice participation last week and were listed as questionable on the Friday injury report.

The Vikings signed Beckham on Wednesday with Jefferson and Addison ailing and No. 3 receiver Jauan Jennings having caught only two passes on four targets in his first season with the team. 

Speaking Wednesday to reporters in Minnesota, O'Connell recalled how Beckham appeared in a game three days after signing with the Los Angeles Rams during the 2021 season. O'Connell was the Rams' offensive coordinator at the time.

"I've seen him do it before," O'Connell said. "The good thing about our system is we've got some mechanisms that either he can quickly learn, and know those are absolutes if we need to go that route in the game, if he were to be elevated."

The Vikings have started 4-0 despite an offense that has ranked among the NFL's worst. Jefferson suffered a sprained left ankle in Week 3, missed Week 4 and his available for Sunday's game in New Orleans has yet to be determined.

Beckham, 33, played 19 snaps in three games with the Giants and did not record a catch. Before returning this season, he had played his first five seasons with the franchise after being selected with the No. 12 pick in 2014. Beckham was hoping to resuscitate his career after not playing in the NFL since the 2024 season, when he caught just nine passes for 54 yards with the Dolphins.

Beckham has also played for the Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens. He has 575 catches for 7,987 yards with 59 touchdowns in his career.

articles.headline: Vinícius Júnior 'sorry' after red card for hair pull; Mourinho skips Madrid presser
articles.description: Vinícius Júnior has apologized to his Real Madrid teammates and fans after being red-carded for pulling an opponent's hair in a dramatic, off-the-bench cameo during his team's LaLiga win over Villarreal on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィニシウス・ジュニオール、髪を引っ張りレッドカードを受けたことを謝罪。ムリーニョは記者会見を欠席
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日のラ・リーガ、ビジャレアル戦で勝利したレアル・マドリードのヴィニシウス・ジュニオールが、途中出場から相手選手の髪を引っ張ったことでレッドカードを受けた。彼はチームメイトとファンに謝罪した。
articles.body:
MADRID -- Vinícius Júnior has apologized to his Real Madrid teammates and fans after being red-carded for pulling an opponent's hair in a dramatic, off-the-bench cameo during his team's LaLiga win over Villarreal on Saturday.

Vinícius was celebrating scoring what he thought was Madrid's second goal when it was ruled out following a video review and he was instead sent off after replays showed he had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up.

"The joy remains. Sorry to my team and the fans," Vinícius posted on Instagram following the game.

- Vinícius Júnior benched as Real Madrid take on Villarreal

- Atlético Madrid mock Real Madrid on social media over Federico Valverde recovery

- Kylian Mbappé to start for Real Madrid, criticism 'ridiculous' - José Mourinho

However, the decision sparked an angry reaction from the Madrid bench. Coach José Mourinho later skipped his scheduled post-match news conference.

The Brazil international was left out of the starting XI by Mourinho -- replaced by Yan Diomande -- after the coach admitted that the forward has been unable to find his best form this season.

Vinícius was introduced on 52 minutes with the game tied at 0-0, with Diomande opening the scoring at the Bernabéu 10 minutes later.

Vinícius then looked to have made a decisive contribution when he converted Jude Bellingham's pass to make it 2-0, with Mourinho sprinting onto the pitch to celebrate with his players.

However a VAR check showed he had pulled Saliba's hair as he raced forwards. The goal was overturned, and referee Isidro Díaz de Mera showed Vinícius a straight red card.

"I don't understand what's happening with the referees, with the red card. I don't understand it," midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni told Real Madrid TV.

The referee's report said Vinicius had "disputed the [red card] decision, shouting, moving towards me with an aggressive attitude, and having to be restrained by his teammates."

Villarreal defender Juan Foyth had a different view of the incident.

"I don't think he meant to hurt anyone but it is a red card," the Argentina international said.

The star's punishment will be confirmed this week by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary panel, but Madrid have just one more league game -- against Sevilla on Oct. 18 -- before they travel to Barcelona for El Clásico on Oct. 25.

Although, the decision left 10-man Madrid to nervously defend a narrow lead in the game's closing stages, Mourinho's side saw out the 1-0 win.

The result leaves Real Madrid in third place in the LaLiga standings, a point behind Atlético Madrid and six points behind leaders Barcelona.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Christian McCaffrey, Olivia Culpo announce birth of second child
articles.description: McCaffrey and his wife, Olivia Culpo, announced the news of the birth of their second child in a joint post on Instagram on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: クリスチャン・マキャフリーとオリビア・カルポ、第2子の誕生を発表
articles.descriptionJa: マキャフリーと妻のオリビア・カルポは土曜日、Instagramの共同投稿で第2子が誕生したことを報告した。
articles.body:
Christian McCaffrey and Olivia Culpo have welcomed their second child, the couple announced Saturday.

McCaffrey, a running back for the San Francisco 49ers, and Culpo, an actress and former Miss Universe, made a joint post on Instagram announcing the news, with the carousel including 10 photos of the newborn, the couple and their eldest child, Colette Annalise, who was born in July 2025. The post's caption reveals the baby boy's name -- Roman Augustus McCaffrey -- and his date of birth: Sept. 29.

The couple had announced back in May that they would be expecting another child -- the "best birthday gift" for Culpo.

McCaffery and Culpo have been married since 2024, with the two having met on a blind date in 2019.

articles.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 5, which kicked off Thursday night with a game between the Buccaneers and Cowboys.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday. 

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

articles.headline: Knicks' Towns opens up about grief for World Mental Health Day
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns shared his emotional journey following the death of his mother six years ago to mark World Mental Health Day on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ニックスのタウンズ、世界メンタルヘルスデーに際し喪失感について語る
articles.descriptionJa: カール＝アンソニー・タウンズは土曜日の世界メンタルヘルスデーに際し、6年前に母親を亡くした後の感情的な道のりについて明かした。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Karl-Anthony Towns has been traded from Minnesota, lost the conference finals and won the NBA title for his childhood team -- and still feels he is in the period of grief that began six years ago.

Just 10 days before the New York Knicks' banner-raising celebration, the All-Star big man marked World Mental Health Day by sharing his ongoing emotional journey following the death of his mother to complications from COVID-19.

Entering the first game of this year's NBA Finals, he said he felt "this very big calm" wash over him. He was taken back to amateur youth games with crowds so small he could spot his mom from anywhere.

"I felt like it was kind of just me, her and the game of basketball," he told the audience gathered Saturday by the nonprofit Project Healthy Minds. "I was able to be like an artist out there. I was able to have my paint brush and have a canvas with the court. And I was able to just paint a beautiful picture for her about the love I have for the game. The love I have to show the world because of her."

There was a time when he had lost that love for the game. Towns, whose bright smile became a constant image of the Knicks' championship run, said basketball "felt hollow" after his mother's death. "I didn't know if I wanted to do it anymore," he said.

But Towns found some solace in Arnie Kander, a well-known strength and wellness coach.

"Just to be heard, to be able to talk to someone you can trust, be able to really unload all that pain onto it and allow them to understand your feelings and articulate your feelings the right way, it makes life much lighter," he said. "And I felt myself getting lighter every time we kept talking."

Athletes embrace mental health Project Healthy Minds hopes Towns' example will inspire others to seek mental health care. The tech nonprofit runs a free online marketplace for finding therapy, psychiatry, support groups and other services. Its annual World Mental Health Day festival in New York offers an all-day schedule of yoga, art therapy and speakers.

Speaking Saturday with Towns was Boardroom CEO Rich Kleiman, the longtime manager for NBA superstar Kevin Durant and a new member of Project Healthy Minds' board.

Kleiman told The Associated Press that these sorts of conversations are growing more prevalent among athletes. DeMar DeRozan and Kevin Love kick-started the conversation eight years ago when DeRozan tweeted about depression and Love then published a first-person essay about anxiety. Kleiman recalled trading stories about anxiety attacks with Love for several hours one night shortly afterward.

Most players won't feel that comfortable constantly telling their story, Kleiman said. Mental health isn't a topic of discussion in the locker room. But he said players are certainly more aware of its impact.

articles.headline: Rams: Myles Garrett making 'good progress,' but no return timeline
articles.description: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett is "making good progress" in his recovery from knee surgery, coach Sean McVay said, but the team is unlikely to open his 21-day practice window next week.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズ：マイルズ・ギャレットは「順調に進展」しているが復帰時期は未定
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・ラムズのディフェンシブエンド、マイルズ・ギャレットは膝の手術からの回復が「順調に進展」しているとショーン・マクベイ監督は語ったが、来週中に21日間の練習期間を開始する可能性は低い。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett is "making good progress" in his recovery from knee surgery, coach Sean McVay said, but the team is unlikely to open his 21-day practice window next week.

Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year, had arthroscopic surgery on his knee in mid-September and was placed on injured reserve. Garrett played in the Rams' season opener but said after the game that he was not 100% healthy.

"His surgery went really well," McVay said Saturday. "He's making good progress. As far as what that timeline looks like, it's kind of week-to-week in terms of how he feels. But I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week."

McVay has been hesitant to put a timeline on Garrett's return from injured reserve but said Saturday that the focus now is making sure Garrett can get back to "return to performance" rather than just "return to play."

Garrett missed most of training camp while dealing with what McVay called irritation in Garrett's knee.

"So hopefully that's gone and it's really just how quickly can the alien get up to speed for us," McVay said. "But no, I think because we got that fixed and because he's feeling so good, I think that'll be an accelerated process. But him actually doing football-related activities and drills will be very important for us to put him in a position to join the group and be the guy that we're accustomed to seeing. And that he wants to be for this team as well."

The Rams traded for Garrett this offseason, sending two-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Jared Verse and three draft picks, including a first-round selection in 2027, to the Cleveland Browns. The pass rusher set the single-season sack record with 23 last season for the Browns.

articles.headline: Patriots place veteran WR Mack Hollins on IR with calf injury
articles.description: The Patriots placed veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins on injured reserve Saturday with a calf injury.
articles.headlineJa: ペイトリオッツ、ベテランWRのマック・ホリンズをふくらはぎの負傷でIRに登録
articles.descriptionJa: ペイトリオッツは土曜日、ベテランワイドレシーバーのマック・ホリンズをふくらはぎの負傷により負傷者リスト（IR）に登録した。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins, whose role expanded when the team lost No. 1 target A.J. Brown to a high-ankle sprain in the season opener, was placed on injured reserve Saturday.

Hollins hopped off the field on his right foot in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over the Buffalo Bills, with the club announcing he had a calf injury.

Hollins leads the team with 15 receptions and 209 receiving yards, and now the Patriots (2-2) will have just four receivers -- Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams -- on their roster for Sunday's home game against the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders (1 p.m., CBS). 

Brown, who has been more visible in the locker room in recent weeks when reporters have been present, is eligible to be designated for return from IR next week.

Hollins, in his 10th NFL season, said Wednesday: "I'm working as hard as I can to get back as fast as I can. As a veteran, you have to stay out of your own way sometimes."

In addition to Hollins, the club placed veteran fullback Reggie Gilliam on injured reserve, marking the 19th player the Patriots have put on IR -- already exceeding the total from 2025 in a surprise run to the Super Bowl.

The Patriots also announced that special teams ace Brenden Schooler was activated from the non-football injury list, and seven-year veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor was signed to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. Vildor's signing was necessary because the Patriots have already ruled out four cornerbacks, including starters Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III, for Sunday's game.

Veteran linebacker K.J. Britt and rookie safety Elliott Davison were also elevated from the practice squad for the game, with their primary contributions likely to come on special teams.
